note: Adding bounded Ollama drafting put a second stdlib HTTP client in engine.py. The constitution audit had encoded the older implementation detail that ollama_embed.py was the only operator-local client, so it changed CONST-0-3 from differently governed to FAILS even though the new client refuses every non-loopback host.

decisions.question: How should the constitution audit classify explicitly configured operator-local Ollama clients?
decisions.commitment: As differently governed, not satisfied and not failing. The operator grants the local reach by installing and starting Ollama; Nestor does not mint fleet egress. The audit recognizes the two named Ollama client modules, while runtime refusal tests enforce the drafting client's loopback-only host boundary.
decisions.why: CONST-0-3 forbids an agent extending its own reach. A configured local daemon is still a network-shaped mechanism, so calling it satisfied would erase the constitutional distinction; calling it a failure would claim off-machine reach that the drafting client refuses before opening a socket.

decisions.question: What keeps the local-client classification from becoming a blanket network exemption?
decisions.commitment: The source probe fails if any unclassified module contains an HTTP client, and its regression test adds a rogue requests.get call and asserts FAILS. The recognized set is exactly engine.py and ollama_embed.py; adding another network client is red by default.
decisions.why: The defect was a stale one-file allowlist, not a reason to stop detecting new reach. A bounded named set plus a forbidden-act test updates the known mechanism while preserving the tripwire for every future client.
